Record Class ChromaticText.Style

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.ChromaticText.Style
Record Components:
color - custom RGB, or null to leave color selection to the renderer
font - effect identity, or null; no separate font texture is required
effect - active primary callback, or null
outline - outline RGB, or null when no outline is active
vanillaColor - vanilla palette index, or -1 when no vanilla color is selected
flags - five bits for the k/l/m/n/o vanilla styles, respectively
colorCode - original custom color token needed to reconstruct state
effectCode - original primary effect token needed to reconstruct state
outlineCode - original outline token needed to reconstruct state
segment - raw start of the primary effect segment, or -1 for the default state
decorator - separate outline-effect callback, or null
Enclosing class:
ChromaticText
public static record ChromaticText.Style(Integer color, net.minecraft.util.ResourceLocation font, IChromaticEffect effect, Integer outline, int vanillaColor, int flags, String colorCode, String effectCode, String outlineCode, int segment, IChromaticEffect decorator) extends Record
Carries all formatting state needed to draw a glyph and continue it on another line.

  • Method Details

    • bold

      public boolean bold()
      Tests the vanilla bold bit used when calculating character advance.
      Returns:
      true when the second style bit is set

    • prefix

      public String prefix()
      Builds the compatibility prefix in its fixed color/effect/outline order.

      Reparsing a primary effect clears a custom color emitted before it. This prefix can therefore lose a custom color that was originally applied after an effect, while keeping the effect itself. Reverse trimming and wrapped continuations use this sequence; it does not round-trip every mixed color/effect style.

      Returns:
      reset, vanilla color, custom color/effect/outline tokens and vanilla style flags in emission order

    • vanillaPrefix

      public String vanillaPrefix()
      Restores only the vanilla subset before passing one visible glyph to FontRenderer.

      Custom state is supplied separately through the render context, avoiding recursive interpretation of the same custom token for every glyph pass.

      Returns:
      reset plus the selected vanilla color and style flags
